Principal Risk Types:
Credit risk
Potential for loss due to the failure of a counterparty to
meet its agreed obligations to pay the Group.
How these are managed:
The Group manages its credit exposures following the
principle of diversification across products, client segments
and industry sectors.

Principal Risk Types:
Traded risk
Potential for loss of economic value due to adverse
changes in financial market rates or prices.
How these are managed:
The Group controls its trading portfolio and activities to
ensure that market risk losses (financial or reputational) do
not cause material damage to the Group’s franchise.

Principal Risk Types:
Capital & Liquidity risk
Capital: potential for insufficient level or composition of
capital to support our normal activities.
Liquidity: potential for failure where we may not have
sufficient stable or diverse sources of funding or financial
resources to meet our obligations as they fall due.
How these are managed:
The Group maintains a strong capital position including the
maintenance of management buffers sufficient to support its
strategic aims and holds an adequate buffer of high quality
liquid assets to survive extreme but plausible liquidity stress
scenarios for at least 60 days without recourse to
extraordinary central bank support.

Principal Risk Types:
Operational risk
Potential for loss from inadequate or failed internal
processes and systems, human error, or from the impact
of external events (including legal risks).
How these are managed:
The Group controls operational risks to ensure that
operational losses (financial or reputational), including any
related to conduct of business matters, do not cause material
damage to the franchise.

Principal Risk Types:
Reputational risk
Potential for damage to the franchise, resulting in loss of
earnings or adverse impact on market capitalisation,
because of stakeholders taking a negative view of the
organisation, its actions or inactions – leading its
stakeholders to change their behaviour.
How these are managed:
The Group protects the franchise from material damage to its
reputation by ensuring that any business activity is
satisfactorily assessed and managed by the appropriate level
of management and governance oversight.
